first_impression.reaction: Googled 'best time to get married in greece' on the train. The first line tells me there's no single answer, which is a bit of a 'just tell me' moment, but then it gives me the four things that decide it and promises month by month. Fair enough. I'd hit the takeaways, look for a quick shortlist, check the table, then jump to the 'which months suit your wedding' bit. The problem is that bit is way down the page.

journey.quote: When to get married in Greece has no single answer, and any guide that names one month for every couple is guessing.
journey.reaction: Slightly annoying when I typed 'best time', but honestly I trust it more than a page that just says 'June!'. At least it's straight with me.

journey.quote: The months that work for you depend on four things: the island, how well your guests cope with heat, whether you want a church ceremony, and how long everyone will stay.
journey.reaction: Good, that's the actual framework in one sentence. I know what I'm deciding on.

journey.quote: Weather in Greece differs by island, so read each figure against its station: Naxos for the Cyclades, Heraklion and Chania Souda for Crete, Rodos for Rhodes and Kerkyra for Corfu.
journey.reaction: First takeaway is a list of weather stations. On my phone that's the one line I wanted to be a quick steer, like 'June and September are warm and dry without peak heat'. I don't care which station it is yet.

journey.quote: The Greek Orthodox Archdiocese of Australia lists dates when marriages are not permitted, including Great Lent to Easter Sunday and 1 to 15 August.
journey.reaction: Didn't know that at all. Mid-August is off for a church wedding? That's genuinely useful and I'd tell my fiance.

journey.section: How to read the weather figures
journey.quote: These are long-term monthly averages, not forecasts. The Rodos and Heraklion figures cover 1955 to 2010, Chania Souda covers 1958 to 2010 and Kerkyra covers 1955 to 2010.
journey.reaction: A whole section of data periods and station heights before I even get to the months. I scrolled straight past this.

journey.section: Greece wedding weather by month, April to October
journey.quote: Each cell shows the average maximum temperature, then the average number of rain days.
journey.reaction: Real numbers, which I like. But six columns with two numbers per cell is going to be sideways scrolling on my phone. I'd probably screenshot it and zoom.

journey.section: Greece wedding weather by month, April to October
journey.quote: June to August is the dry core everywhere except Corfu, which keeps three to five rain days a month through summer.
journey.reaction: This is the line I actually needed. Short and clear. Should be up top.

journey.quote: As at November 2026, [Smartraveller](https://www.smartraveller.gov.au/destinations/europe/greece) says heatwaves are frequent in Greece over the summer months and can cause heat exhaustion, heat stroke and death.
journey.reaction: Dated this month and from a government site. That answers my 'is this still true?' worry.

journey.quote: For a July wedding, that shapes the day: an evening ceremony, shade for the aperitivo, water at every seat, and shorter excursions for older guests.
journey.reaction: Practical, I can picture it. My grandma would need exactly this.

journey.quote: The Naxos station records a prevailing north wind in every month, and its wind power reading rises from 10.3 in June to 13.3 in July.
journey.reaction: 10.3 to 13.3 of what? I don't know what that number means. 'It gets windier' would do.

journey.quote: **A sunset ceremony in the Cyclades.** The Naxos station shows the mildest summer maximums in this guide, at 25.9 to 27.1°C from June to August, and almost no rain.
journey.reaction: This is the section I came for. Pick my situation, get my months. Love it. I just had to scroll past seven months, four islands and a holiday list to find it.

journey.quote: There is no month that suits every wedding. These scenarios match common priorities to the figures above.
journey.reaction: This heading matches my search better than anything else on the page, and it's near the bottom. Felt buried.

journey.quote: Is October too late for a Greek island wedding?
journey.reaction: Exactly a question I'd ask. Direct answer, 'Not for many venues, but plan for rain.' Good FAQ.

journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is your single point of contact, matching your shortlisted months to venue availability, travel and guest stays, working in your time zone and quoting in AUD, with the fee agreed in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: Quoting in AUD makes me think this is for Australians. Fee in writing sounds above board though.

unanswered_questions: Do you work with couples who aren't based in Australia, for example in Singapore?
What does the Naxos 'wind power reading' number actually measure?
If I want a church wedding in Greece rather than Australia, are the closed dates the same?

turn_offs_found.quote: Weather in Greece differs by island, so read each figure against its station: Naxos for the Cyclades, Heraklion and Chania Souda for Crete, Rodos for Rhodes and Kerkyra for Corfu.
turn_offs_found.why: The takeaways are all I read first on the phone, and the first one tells me about weather stations instead of giving me a steer on months. The page has a great plain summary ('June to August is the dry core everywhere except Corfu') but it's halfway down.

turn_offs_found.quote: There is no month that suits every wedding. These scenarios match common priorities to the figures above.
turn_offs_found.why: The scenario section is the closest thing to an answer to 'best time', and it sits after the full month-by-month, island and holiday sections. Answer buried below a long body is exactly what makes me leave.

turn_offs_found.quote: These are long-term monthly averages, not forecasts. The Rodos and Heraklion figures cover 1955 to 2010, Chania Souda covers 1958 to 2010 and Kerkyra covers 1955 to 2010.
turn_offs_found.why: Methodology before the answer. It's the kind of scroll-through I fear on a phone. Fine to keep, but it doesn't need to come before the table.

would_share_with: My fiance, for the Orthodox closed dates and the scenario list
My mum, for the July heat advice about older guests

cta_reaction.quote: Once you have two or three months in mind, a [Wedded Concierge consultation](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=best-time-to-get-married-in-greece&utm_content=primary) turns them into dates a venue can actually hold.
cta_reaction.why: I like that it's low-key and says 'once you have two or three months in mind', which isn't pushy. But I'm still at the 'which month' stage and 'quoting in AUD' makes me unsure they're for me. I'd bookmark the page and maybe come back.

top_3_changes: Replace or lead the Key takeaways with a plain month steer drawn from the existing copy, e.g. 'June to August is the dry core everywhere except Corfu' plus a pointer to the 'Which months suit your wedding' scenarios, and move the station list lower.
Move 'Which months suit your wedding' up, directly after the table (or link to it from the intro), so the section that best matches the search sits within one scroll.

Move 'How to read the weather figures' below the table or collapse it to one line, and explain the Naxos wind power reading in plain words (or just say it gets windier) so the numbers make sense on a phone.

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Stayed in character as Priya, a casual Google searcher on a phone

Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection

assumptions: Persona is provisional (weight 0.10); reactions reflect generic informational search intent.

Arrived from a Google search for 'best time to get married in greece' on a phone with a 5-minute budget; read the intro, takeaways, table and summary, July, the scenario section and FAQ, and skimmed the methodology, other months, island sections and holidays.

The 'no single answer' framing is logged as a low-severity objection only, since the guide deliberately names no best month; the requested fix is ordering and surfacing existing content, not adding a verdict.
Image slots and HTML comments treated as invisible.
